## What changed or decided
Most of the implementation was already present in the worktree from a prior session and is correct; I verified it end-to-end and closed the one remaining gap.

- **`scripts/mergegate_check.py`** (pre-existing, verified correct): `normal_task_contract_immutability_reasons()` freezes the seven governance fields (`scope, non_goals, required_skills, risk_level, locks, acceptance_checks, test_command`) to the base snapshot on the normal path, base-when-present resolution, fail-closed on a changed own-task-file with no base, first-registration passes. `resolved_guardian_risk_never_weaker()` resolves the Guardian risk as `max(base, head)` so a self-lowered `risk_level` cannot dissolve the gate. The mutable set reuses the single ADR 0017 constant `_CLOSEOUT_MUTABLE_TASK_FIELDS` (not re-declared); the frozen set is the explicit 7, not the complement (so loop-written `pre_pr_code_review`/`cca_rerun_count` still ride the impl-PR head). Call sites live only in the `elif resolved_task_id` normal-path branch — mutually exclusive with reconcile/contract/post_merge — and the guardian floor is guarded by `task is not None`, so no double-report.
- **`scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh`** (my fix — this file is in my locks): line-1317 `assert_ready("current-task", …)` mutated the own task file's `scope`, which the new rule now correctly **blocks** → the suite broke under `set -e`. I repurposed `current_task_changed` to move a mutable field (`closeout_pr`; status left `review` so it isn't classed as a closeout) keeping `assert_ready`, and added `current_task_governance_changed` with `assert_blocked(…, "frozen governance field 'scope'")`. Avoided the `expected_pr`/`expected_branch` consistency-gate trap.
